cards.front: Tooth: Which tissue covers the dentin of the crown?
cards.back:
Enamel
Why: it is the hardest tissue of the body and protects the crown against wear.

cards.front: Tooth: Which tissue covers the dentin of the root?
cards.back:
Cementum
Why: the periodontal ligament fibres anchor in it, holding the tooth in the alveolar bone.

cards.front: Tooth: What is the difference between enamel and dentin?
cards.back:
Enamel: no cells, cannot regrow, covers the crown.
Dentin: contains tubules with cell processes from the pulp, forms the bulk of the tooth.

cards.text: The {{c1::pulp}} contains nerves and blood vessels and continues into the root as the {{c2::root canal}}.
The tooth is held in the {{c1::alveolar bone}} by the periodontal ligament, which anchors in the {{c2::cementum}}.
